content:
Using multiple devices with Signal? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to access the app across different iPhones and more devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, no longer limited to setting up a secondary mobile device as an iPad.

The company also announced Android linking support today, stating: "We are expanding the linked devices feature on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, and we have always supported iPad."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their full conversation history and media saved within the past 45 days.

Signal stated that the entire transfer process uses end-to-end encryption and the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPad and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac).

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who need to use both personal and work iPhones simultaneously, or for those testing multiple devices.

This move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, which allows users to seamlessly access conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now rolling out on the App Store. Signal also recently introduced a username feature, allowing users to make connections without sharing their phone numbers.
